confirmed.title: Re-selecting the already-selected item is not a selection event, so the source that selected LAST can lose the Inspector
confirmed.where: Task 2 (SelectionEdge, Step 4) + Task 4 Step 6 (per-frame sync) + Task 6 Step 4 (Select* bump only on change)
confirmed.claim: Spec A 3.1 keys the Inspector on 'the source that selected LAST'. The plan turns a selection into an event only when the KEY changes: `SelectionEdge::Observe` returns `!key.empty() && key != lastKey` (plan :817-826), the document sync fires only when `SelectionEpoch()` moved (plan :1585-1593), and Task 6's `SelectAction`/`SelectBinding`/`SelectPart` bump the epoch only when the id differs (plan :2120-2135, pinned by the test 'SelectMap(map) // no change: no bump' at :2027-2028). Consequence: with the document page showing, clicking MeshCube again in the Outliner (already the primary) or, with the scene page showing, clicking the already-selected Jump row does nothing -- the user must select something ELSE or use Back. The mockup the spec was approved on calls setSource on every click (its selectEntity/selectDoc handlers), i.e. a re-click IS a selection. The scene side has no signal at all: `SelectionContext::Select` just assigns (SelectionContext.hpp:36-40) and every Outliner/Viewport click calls it unconditionally (EditorPanels.cpp:1980, :2000, :2009, :2071; EditorAppFrame.cpp:3523).
confirmed.evidence: Spec A 3.1: 'The Inspector shows the page of the source that selected LAST.' Plan :817-826 (`const bool event = !key.empty() && key != lastKey;`), :2027-2028, :2127-2135, :1583-1593; ArcaneEditor/src/Scene/SelectionContext.hpp:36-40; ArcaneEditor/src/Panels/EditorPanels.cpp:1980/2000/2009/2071 (sel.Select on click, no equality test).
confirmed.fix: Make a selection ACT the event, not a key change. (1) Task 3/4: add `std::uint64_t Generation() const` to SelectionContext, incremented in Select()/Toggle()/Clear() unconditionally (all ten call sites are click/command paths -- EditorApp.cpp:1227, EditorAppFrame.cpp:3523, EditorAppProject.cpp:222, EditorAppScene.cpp:493, EditorPanels.cpp:1980-2169 -- none per-frame); change `SelectionEdge::Observe(key)` to `Observe(key, generation)` = `generation != lastGeneration && !key.empty()`, and update the Task 2 'SelectionEdge' case to 'the same key with a new generation IS an event'. (2) Task 6: make SelectMap/SelectAction/SelectBinding/SelectPart bump `selectionEpoch_` on EVERY call (drop the 'no change: no bump' CHECK at :2027-2028 and the `changed` guards at :2120-2135); RestoreSelection/Open re-reports are absorbed by the host's navigation-echo rule (:951-952), which the existing 'history back/forward' case already exercises at :674-675. (3) Task 2 header comment :814-816 and the InspectorHost.hpp preamble: replace 'the same key twice is not [an event]' with 'a selection act that yields the same key is still an event; only an empty key is not'. Add a Task 4 desk line: 'with the document page showing, click the already-selected entity in the Outliner: the Inspector returns to Scene > <name>'.

verdict.reason: Confirmed from the plan text, the spec's mockup and the repo. (1) The plan makes a selection an event only on a KEY change: `SelectionEdge::Observe` returns `!key.empty() && key != lastKey` (plan :829-834) with the header comment "the same key twice is not [an event]" (:824-825), pinned by the test `CHECK_FALSE(edge.Observe("7"))` (:625); the per-frame sync feeds it `m_sceneSource.SelectionKey()` = the primary entity's decimal (:1282-1285, :1592-1593), and the document lane fires only when `SelectionEpoch()` moved (:1596-1601), while Task 6's `SelectMap/SelectAction/SelectBinding/SelectPart` bump only on a differing id (:2131-2147) with the test `model.SelectMap(map); // no change: no bump` (:2036-2037). (2) The scene side has no other signal: `SelectionContext::Select` just assigns (ArcaneEditor/src/Scene/SelectionContext.hpp:35-39) and every Outliner/Viewport click calls it unconditionally (EditorPanels.cpp:1980/2000/2009/2071, EditorAppFrame.cpp:3523). So with a document current, re-clicking the already-primary entity yields key "7" -> "7": no event, `m_current` stays the document, and the Inspector does not return to Scene; symmetric for re-clicking the already-selected Jump row while the scene page shows. (3) Spec A 3.1 says "the source that selected LAST" (spec :50), and the mockup the spec cites (:4) treats every click as a selection: `selectEntity(id){ state.sceneSel=id; ...; setSource({kind:'scene',id}); }` and `selectDoc(sel){ ...; setSource({kind:'doc',...}); }` with no equality guard, so a re-click moves the Inspector there. The plan's "same key twice is not an event" is a deliberate narrowing that contradicts the approved behaviour, and nothing elsewhere in the plan (no re-click/already-selected text anywhere; the desk lists at :1632 and :4041 do not exercise it) compensates. A fresh executor would ship it as written.
verdict.correctedFix: The proposed fix is right in direction; complete it as follows. (1) SelectionContext (Task 3/4): add `std::uint64_t Generation() const noexcept` and bump it in Select(), Toggle() AND AddRange() (SelectionContext.hpp:60-70 -- the Shift-range click is also a selection act the reviewer's list omits) and Clear(); explicitly do NOT bump in Prune() (SelectionContext.hpp:81-90), which EditorApp runs once per frame -- a bump there would re-notify the scene every frame. All Select/Toggle/AddRange/Clear call sites are one-shot click/command paths (EditorApp.cpp:1227, EditorAppFrame.cpp:2511/2519/3521/3523/3532, EditorAppProject.cpp:222, EditorAppScene.cpp:137/493, EditorPanels.cpp:1404-2169), so no per-frame guard is needed. (2) Task 2: change `SelectionEdge` to `struct SelectionEdge { std::uint64_t lastGeneration = 0; bool Observe(std::string_view key, std::uint64_t generation) { const bool event = generation != lastGeneration && !key.empty(); lastGeneration = generation; return event; } };`, rewrite the :621-628 test to the two-argument form (`Observe("7",1)` true, `Observe("7",1)` false [same frame, no act], `Observe("7",2)` TRUE [re-click is an act], `Observe("",3)` false, `Observe("7",4)` true), and replace the :824-825 / :805-811 comments with "a selection ACT that yields the same key is still an event; only an empty key (a clear) is not". Task 4 Step 6 becomes `m_sceneSelectionEdge.Observe(m_sceneSource.SelectionKey(), m_selection.Generation())`. (3) Task 6 Step 4: make all four Select* bump `selectionEpoch_` unconditionally (drop the `changed`/`!=` guards at :2131-2147). Adjust the test at :2033-2040: delete the "no change: no bump" CHECK, and note that the row-click handlers call two or three setters per click (plan :3052-3055, :3716-3727; InputActionsDocumentWidgets.cpp:163/180/190) so the epoch advances by more than one per click -- change the exact-count CHECKs (`== e0 + 1`, `== e0 + 3`) to `>` comparisons or to the actual counts (SelectMap x2 + SelectAction + SelectBinding = e0 + 4). The sync only tests `epoch != last` (:1598), so multi-bumps are harmless. RestoreSelection/GoBack re-reports still land on the cursor entry and are absorbed by Push's navigation-echo rule (:958-961), exercised at :674-676. (4) Add a Task 4 Step 7 desk line: "(7) open Player.arcinput, click Jump (Inspector shows the document), then click the already-selected MeshCube in the Outliner: the Inspector returns to Scene > MeshCube; the reverse (scene page showing, re-click Jump) returns to the document."

confirmed.title: TryCompileSinglePath: `return { Source, code };` does not compile for std::optional<ControlId>

verdict.reason: Confirmed from the plan and the source. Plan D:/dev/starworks/Arcane/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-28-inspector-ownership-and-input-editor.md:1831-1833 declares `std::optional<ControlId> TryCompileSinglePath(...)` and says the body keeps "every `return { Source, code };`". `ControlId` is a plain aggregate `{ ControlSource source; uint32_t code; }` (ArcaneClient/src/Arcane/Input/InputActions.cpp:74-78), and the current `ControlId CompileSinglePath` returns braced pairs at :211, :224, :230-232, :240, :253, :258, :263. A two-element braced-init-list cannot copy-list-initialise `std::optional<ControlId>`: optional is not an aggregate and has no non-explicit two-parameter constructor (the only two-arg-capable one is the explicit `in_place_t, Args...`, whose first parameter cannot take a `ControlSource`), so every one of those seven returns is a hard compile error under the plan text as written. The proposed fix is correct and sufficient: `return ControlId{ Source, code };` converts through optional's non-explicit `U&&` constructor, and `return ControlId{};` keeps the empty-path case a silent None.

refuted.title: The 'every offered picker path compiles to a resolved binding' property is tested against the same function that generates the list
refuted.reason: The check is not circular in the sense claimed, and there is no "later" evaluator step that can zero-compile a path the compile step accepted. In the repository, LoadAsset's only compile gate is `cb.chord = CompilePath(cb.path, mapName, actionName)` (InputActions.cpp:611), and CompilePath does nothing but split on '+' and call CompileSinglePath per part (:279-303). After the plan's refactor (plan :1831-1841) CompileSinglePath is `TryCompileSinglePath` + one ARC_WARN, so `IsKnownControlPath` (plan :1924-1937, `TryCompileSinglePath(part)`) invokes the identical resolution LoadAsset stores -- including the non-table parts of the compiler: the `<Device>/` framing parse, the `scancode/` prefix handling and the SDL_GetScancodeFromName / SDL_GetKeyFromName library lookups for the Keyboard branch (InputActions.cpp:198-227), and the `button/N` 1..5 range for Mouse (:236-245). Hoisting the three tables (plan :1966) does not collapse the test to table-vs-table: a table entry whose SDL spelling SDL rejects, or a KnownControls emission that mis-frames the path, still fails `TryCompileSinglePath`. For Gamepad, the token tables ARE the compiler's resolution (:250-262), so "the tables accept it but the evaluator zero-compiles it" is not a reachable state; ResolveControl (:308+) consumes a typed ControlId and has no further zero-ing gate. The spec's property (spec B :91 "never offer a path the evaluator cannot compile", :124-125 "every offered path compiles to a resolved binding") is a compile-level property, which this test proves against the real compiler. The five hygiene-pass paths were picker-vs-compiler drift in a hand-kept editor list -- exactly what this loop detects. The proposed fix would add a LoadAsset round-trip through the same function and, moreover, cites a "log capture" shape that InputActionsTest.cpp does not have (the :97-109 case only observes `Down("ghost")` == false; no ARC_WARN capture exists in the file), so it is also not executable as written. Not a defect.
